items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider the integral
[MATH: \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits}
\newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits}]

Content:
[MATH: \int \csch^2(2x+3) \, \textrm{d}x.]

Content:
As it is, this integral doesn't resemble any of the basic integrals we have encountered so far. However, it is very similar to the basic integral for the hyperbolic cotangent,

Content:
[MATH: \int \csch^2 u \, \textrm{d}u = -\coth u+C.]

Content:
The only difference is that instead of [MATH: u] as the variable, we have [MATH: 2x+3.]

Content:
So, let [MATH: u=2x+3.] Differentiating, we have

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2} \, \textrm{d}u.]

Content:
Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: ∫csch^{2} (2x + 3)dx|= ∫csch^{2} u ⋅ (1)/(2)du; = (1)/(2)∫csch^{2} udu; = (1)/(2)(− \coth u) + C; = − (1)/(2)\coth (2x + 3) + C]

items.title: Integrating Hyperbolic Functions With Linear Arguments

sections.normalized_html: Evaluate the integral [MATH: \displaystyle ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \int_{-2}^{1} \sinh {\left(2x+1 ight)} \, extrm{d}x.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: u=2x+1.] Differentiating, we have [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm d x=\dfrac 1 2 \, \textrm d u.]

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from [MATH: x] to [MATH: u.] [MATH: x|− 2|1; u|− 3|3]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and evaluate:

[MATH: ∫_{− 2}^{1}\sinh (2x + 1)dx|= ∫_{− 3}^{3}\sinh u ⋅ (1)/(2)du; = (1)/(2)∫_{− 3}^{3}\sinh udu; = (1)/(2)\cosh u|_{− 3}^{3}; = (1)/(2)(\cosh 3 − \cosh (− 3)); = (1)/(2)(\cosh 3 − \cosh 3); = 0]
sections.readable_text:
Let [MATH: u=2x+1.] Differentiating, we have
[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm d x=\dfrac 1 2 \, \textrm d u.]

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from [MATH: x] to [MATH: u.]
[MATH: x|− 2|1; u|− 3|3]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and evaluate:

[MATH: ∫_{− 2}^{1}\sinh (2x + 1)dx|= ∫_{− 3}^{3}\sinh u ⋅ (1)/(2)du; = (1)/(2)∫_{− 3}^{3}\sinh udu; = (1)/(2)\cosh u|_{− 3}^{3}; = (1)/(2)(\cosh 3 − \cosh (− 3)); = (1)/(2)(\cosh 3 − \cosh 3); = 0]

items.title: Integrating Reciprocal Hyperbolic Functions With Linear Arguments

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the integral [MATH: \displaystyle ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \int \csch(3x+1)\coth(3x+1) \, extrm{d}x.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: u=3x+1.] Differentiating, we have

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x =\dfrac{1}{3} \, \textrm{d}u.]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

[MATH: ∫csch (3x + 1)\coth (3x + 1)dx|= ∫csch u\coth u ⋅ (1)/(3)du; = (1)/(3)∫csch u\coth udu; = (1)/(3)(− csch u) + C; = − (1)/(3)csch (3x + 1) + C]
sections.readable_text:
Let [MATH: u=3x+1.] Differentiating, we have

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = 3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x =\dfrac{1}{3} \, \textrm{d}u.]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows:

[MATH: ∫csch (3x + 1)\coth (3x + 1)dx|= ∫csch u\coth u ⋅ (1)/(3)du; = (1)/(3)∫csch u\coth udu; = (1)/(3)(− csch u) + C; = − (1)/(3)csch (3x + 1) + C]

items.title: Integrating Products Containing Hyperbolic Functions Using Substitution

sections.normalized_html: Evaluate the integral [MATH: \displaystyle ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} {\int_{-2}^{2} x^2\sinh{x^3}}\, extrm{d}x.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let [MATH: u=x^3.] Differentiating, we have [MATH: \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}=3x^2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{1}{3}\textrm{d} u = x^2\, \textrm d x.]

Before substituting, we use the table below to change the limits from [MATH: x] to [MATH: u.] [MATH: x|− 2|2; u|− 8|8]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and evaluate: [MATH: \eqalign{ \newcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{\rm arsinh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{\rm arcosh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{\rm artanh}\nolimits} \newcommand{\sech}{\mathop{\rm sech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\csch}{\mathop{\rm csch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\coth}{\mathop{\rm coth}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{\rm arsech}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{\rm arcsch}\nolimits} \newcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{\rm arcoth}\nolimits} \int_{-2}^{2} x^2\sinh{x^3}\, \textrm{d}x &=\int_{-2}^{2} \sinh{x^3}\cdot x^2\,\textrm{d}x\[5pt] &=\int_{-8}^{8} \sinh{u}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}\, \textrm{d}u\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3}\cosh u\Big|_{-8}^{8}\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\cosh{8} - \cosh{(-8)}\right)\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\cosh{8} - \cosh{8}\right)\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{3}\cdot 0\[5pt] &=0 }]

items.title: Integrating Quotients Containing Hyperbolic Functions Using Substitution

sections.normalized_html: Calculate [MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle \int \dfrac{x\sinh{x^2}}{\cosh{x^2}}\, extrm{d}x.]
EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits}]

Let [MATH: u= \cosh{x^2}.] Differentiating, we have [MATH: \dfrac{ extrm{d}u}{ extrm{d}x} = 2x\sinh{x^2} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \dfrac{1}{2} \, extrm{d}u = x\sinh{x^2} \, extrm{d}x.]

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of [MATH: u] and compute it, as follows: [MATH: \eqalign{ ewcommand{\arsinh}{\mathop{ m arsinh} olimits} ewcommand{\arcosh}{\mathop{ m arcosh} olimits} ewcommand{\artanh}{\mathop{ m artanh} olimits} ewcommand{\sech}{\mathop{ m sech} olimits} ewcommand{\csch}{\mathop{ m csch} olimits} ewcommand{\coth}{\mathop{ m coth} olimits} ewcommand{\arsech}{\mathop{ m arsech} olimits} ewcommand{\arcsch}{\mathop{ m arcsch} olimits} ewcommand{\arcoth}{\mathop{ m arcoth} olimits} \displaystyle \int \dfrac{x\sinh{x^2}}{\cosh{x^2}}\, extrm{d}x &= \int \dfrac{1}{\cosh{x^2}}\cdot x\sinh{x^2}\, extrm{d}x\[5pt] &= \int \dfrac{1}{u}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \, extrm d u \[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{1}{u}\, extrm{d}u\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|u|+C\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left(\cosh{x^2} ight)+ C }]
